title: Legend of Hanuma's birth
introduction: Legend of Hanuma's birth is eulogised together with his innate capabilities. Jambavanta familiarises Hanuma of his capabilities giving an account of his birth, rather what for he took birth, and extols his unready faculty. In the sixty-sixth chapter of Bala Kanda, Valmiki very concisely narrates the birth of Seetha. But here Valmiki elaborately informs about the birth of Hanuma through Jambavanta. Some information about Hanuma is included in the endnote.
closing: Apart from trying to snatch Sun-fruit, Hanuma's childhood-rascaling was intolerable for some sages and hermits. Hanuma used to tease and tickle the sages by snatching away their personal belongings, by spoiling well arranged worship articles etc. Knowing that Hanuma is indomitable by the blessings of Brahma and Indra and all the celestials, and as a severe punishment is uncalled for, as he is simple little monkey, the sages gave him a minor curse. That curse is 'Hanuma does not remember his might on his own, but recollects it whenever others remind him about it...' If Hanuma were to be aware of his own might, the course of Ramayana would have been otherwise. He would have simply enlarged his body and brought whole of Lanka island to Rama, as he has lifted sanjivini mountain, to enliven Lakshmana in the war with Ravana's son, Indrajit. So this was a necessary curse upon Hanuma. Hence Jambavanta had to harangue Hanuma.

The word kapi also means 'Sun...' kam= water; pi= drinker, drinker of waters... the Sun. kaparkayebhavānarāḥ Sun, monkey, elephant are the meanings for kapi. As Sun drinks waters only to give rain Hanuma drinks rāma rasa amṛta to shower wisdom on anyone, may it be Sugreeva, Angada or Seetha. Hanuma is the student of a guru no less than Sun-god. On ascertaining that nobody is prepared to teach him scriptures, and fied him as a fickle monkey, he approaches Sun, as Sun is an all-knowing teacher, karma sākśi, an eternal witness of all deeds. Hanuma raises his body to solar orbit and requests Sun to accept his studentship. Sun declines saying, "I am ever on my wheels, where can I be standstill to teach you leisurely, I have my unending duty to perform..." and thus continued His solar traversal. But Hanuma undeterred by Sun's dismissing, still enhances his body, placing one leg on the eastern mountain range and the other on the western, face turned toward the travelling Sun. Hanuma again requested Sun in this posture saying, "my face will always be towards you, in whichever orbit you go, but teach me...oh! God..." Pleased by the pertinence of Hanuma, Sun teaches all the scriptures to Hanuma. So also Hanuma is a witness to all the happenings in Ramayana, like Sun, and also performing whatever duty assigned to him. Even today any student is asked to adore Hanuma, to obtain such a stubborn health, enduring education, and above all a reverential scholarship.

Hanuma is having a benefit of icchā maraṇam 'death at his wish...' but he is not yet dead, believably, for he is ciranjīvi 'eternal entity on earth...' When Rama is crowned as emperor, after his exile and eliminating Ravana, Rama and Seetha gave gifts to all of their friends. When it was turn to Hanuma to choose a gift, shunning the heavens or other higher planes or other things, he asks for living in this mortal world as long as the name Rama is audible. Then Seetha blesses Hanuma with that gift saying " Oh! Hanuma, wherever you are, there will be plenty of fruits and eatables, and further, in villages, public shelters, temples, houses, gardens, cowsheds, cities, and at riversides, crossroads, pilgrimages, water tanks, trunks of banyan trees, and on mountains, caves, peaks and wherever people stroll, your image will be installed, so that you can listen Rama's name, uttered by the people from all corners of the earth..." Thus Hanuma is believed to be still living, as the name of Rama is still audible. He is also called an old monkey living from ages till now, which is reflected in Maha Bharata, when Bhima could not lift the tail of this old monkey, on his way in forests. Even today one can see huge images, statues of Hanuma at all these places, as said by Seetha, either installed ages ago, or recently.

Another parable is told that Hanuma is the first one to script Ramayana on claytablets, recording each and every detail of what Rama did. Having finished his writing he brought those claytablets to Rama, to bless that work. Rama humbly said to Hanuma, "I have not done anything great to be recorded this laboriously... I have done my righteous duty...that's all..." Then Hanuma was upset. Dejected by the slighting away of 'his great deeds as simple acts of duty' by Rama, Hanuma brought those clay tablets to seashore, recited each verse, and broke each tablet on his knee and threw them into sea. This writing is called hanumad ramayana. This work is unavailable from that time. But one tablet came to shore afloat on the sea, which is retrieved during the period of Mahakavi Kalidasa, and hung at a public place to be deciphered by scholars. On that tablet only one foot of a stanza is available. That foot says "Oh! Ravana, those your ten heads, on which you lifted of Mt. Kailah, the abode of Shiva, are now bumped on battlefield by the claws of crows and eagles, know what has happened to your high-headed Decahedral pride, at the hands of virtue..." Kalidasa deciphers this stanza and informs that it is from hanumad ramayana, recorded by Hanuma, but an extinct script. And Kalidasa salutes that clayplate for he is fortunate enough to see at least one stanza of hanumad ramāyana. It is said that none can conclusively narrate about Hanuma, for he is many faceted. He is symbolic for unwavering dedication to righteousness, unstinting performance of entrusted duties, unfailing talents in service. So the tradition holds Hanuma dear...
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे षट् षष्टितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 66th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
अनेक शत साहस्रीम् विषण्णाम् हरि वाहिनीम् |
जांबवान् समुदीक्ष्य एवम् हनुमंतम् अथ अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
aneka śata sāhasrīm viṣaṇṇām hari vāhinīm |
jāmbavān samudīkṣya evam hanumaṃtam atha abravīt
verses.translation: On overseeing the crestfallen monkey-soldiery, which is with many hundreds and thousands of soldiers, then Jambavanta sad this way to Hanuma.

verses.devanagari:
वीर वानर लोकस्य सर्व शास्त्र विदाम् वर |
तूष्णीम् एकांतम् आश्रित्य हनुमन् किम् न जल्पसि
verses.iast:
vīra vānara lokasya sarva śāstra vidām vara |
tūṣṇīm ekāṃtam āśritya hanuman kim na jalpasi
verses.translation: "Oh, valiant one in the world of vanara-s, being an erudite scholar among all the scriptural scholars, Hanuma, why do not you mumble something, why do you resort to a calmly loneliness...

glosses.meaning: in all, scriptures, among scholars, eminent one

verses.devanagari:
हनुमन् हरि राजस्य सुग्रीवस्य समो हि असि |
राम लक्ष्मणयोः च अपि तेजसा च बलेन च
verses.iast:
hanuman hari rājasya sugrīvasya samo hi asi |
rāma lakṣmaṇayoḥ ca api tejasā ca balena ca
verses.translation: "By your brilliance and brawn, oh, Hanuma, you match up to king of monkeys Sugreeva, or even to Rama and Lakshmana, as well...

glosses.meaning: by brilliance, also, by brawn, as well
to Rama, Lakshmana, also, even to
you match up to, you are, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
अरिष्टनेमिनः पुत्रो वैनतेयो महाबलः |
गरुत्मान् इव विख्यात उत्तमः सर्व पक्षिणाम्
verses.iast:
ariṣṭaneminaḥ putro vainateyo mahābalaḥ |
garutmān iva vikhyāta uttamaḥ sarva pakṣiṇām
verses.translation: "The son of Kashyapa Prajapati and Lady Vinata is the best bird among all the birds who is superbly mighty and who is universally renowned as Garuda...

glosses.meaning: Aristanemi, [another name of Kashyapa Prajapati,] son of
Garuda, thus, universally, renowned as - such a bird is there.

verses.devanagari:
बहुशो हि मया दृष्टः सागरे स महाबलः |
भुजगान् उद्धरन् पक्षी महावेगो महायशाः
verses.iast:
bahuśo hi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sāgare sa mahābalaḥ |
bhujagān uddharan pakṣī mahāvego mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: "Iindeed, I have oftentimes seen that highly glorious, rapidly speedy, great mighty bird Garuda, pecking up reptiles from ocean...

glosses.meaning: by me, oftentimes, is seen, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
पक्षयोः यत् बलम् तस्य तावत् भुज बलम् तव |
विक्रमः च अपि वेगः च न ते तेन अपहीयते
verses.iast:
pakṣayoḥ yat balam tasya tāvat bhuja balam tava |
vikramaḥ ca api vegaḥ ca na te tena apahīyate
verses.translation: "Whatever is the strength of his wings, that much is the strength of you arms, and even by the yardsticks of his dash and dare, yours too, are unreprovable...

glosses.meaning: his, of wings, which, might - is there
your, arms, strength of, is that much

verses.devanagari:
बलम् बुद्धिः च तेजः च सत्त्वम् च हरि सत्तम |
विशिष्टम् सर्व भूतेषु किम् आत्मानम् न सज्जसे
verses.iast:
balam buddhiḥ ca tejaḥ ca sattvam ca hari sattama |
viśiṣṭam sarva bhūteṣu kim ātmānam na sajjase
verses.translation: "Oh, forthright monkey, you are the finest among all beings by the dint of your force, faculty, flair, and fortitude... why then is your unreadiness in this task of leaping ocean...

glosses.itrans: balam buddhiH ca tejaH ca sattvam ca
glosses.iast: balam buddhiḥ ca tejaḥ ca sattvam ca
glosses.devanagari: बलं बुद्धिः च तेजः च सत्त्वं च
glosses.meaning: [your] force, faculty, also, flair, also, fortitude, also

verses.devanagari:
अप्सर अप्सरसाम् श्रेष्ठा विख्याता पुंजिकस्थला |
अंजना इति परिख्याता पत्नी केसरिणो हरेः
verses.iast:
apsara apsarasām śreṣṭhā vikhyātā puṃjikasthalā |
aṃjanā iti parikhyātā patnī kesariṇo hareḥ
verses.translation: "Punjikasthala yclept Anjana is the nicest apsara among all apsara-s and she is the wife of Kesari, the monkey...

glosses.meaning: [yclept] Anjana, thus, made, known - known as
of a monkey, of Kesari, wife of.

verses.devanagari:
विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु रूपेणा अप्रतिमा भुवि |
अभिशापात् अभूत् तात कपित्वे काम रूपिणी
verses.iast:
vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu rūpeṇā apratimā bhuvi |
abhiśāpāt abhūt tāta kapitve kāma rūpiṇī
verses.translation: "She who is distinguished for her unparalleled mien in the three worlds, oh, dear boy Hanuma, had to take a rebirth on earth as a monkey who can change her form by her wish, owing to a curse...

glosses.meaning: by mien, [she] not, paralleled - as an unparalleled apsara
in three, worlds, she is distinguished

verses.devanagari:
दुहिता वानर इन्द्रस्य कुंजरस्य महात्मनः |
मानुषम् विग्रहम् कृत्वा रूप यौवन शालिनी
विचित्र माल्य आभरणा कदाचित् क्षौम धारिणी |
अचरत् पर्वतस्य अग्रे प्रावृड् अंबुद सन्निभे
verses.iast:
duhitā vānara indrasya kuṃjarasya mahātmanaḥ |
mānuṣam vigraham kṛtvā rūpa yauvana śālinī
vicitra mālya ābharaṇā kadācit kśauma dhāriṇī |
acarat parvatasya agre prāvṛḍ ambuda sannibhe
verses.translation: "She who took birth as the daughter of great souled monkey chief Kunjara, on assuming a human physique, putting on caparisons of amazing garlands, dressed in silken clothing, and shining forth with rarity of her beauty and nubility, at one time ambled on the top of a mountain like a streak of lightning athwart a black-cloud of rainy season.

glosses.meaning: form [rarity of beauty], nubility, when shining forth with them
rainy season's, black-cloud, similar in shine
streak of lightning, like] parvatasya agre = mountain, on top

verses.devanagari:
तस्या वस्त्रम् विशालाक्ष्याः पीतम् रक्त दशम् शुभम् |
स्थितायाः पर्वतस्य अग्रे मारुतो अपहरत् शनैः
verses.iast:
tasyā vastram viśālākṣyāḥ pītam rakta daśam śubham |
sthitāyāḥ parvatasya agre māruto apaharat śanaiḥ
verses.translation: "When she is strolling on the mountaintop Air-god has slowly lifted up that broad-eyed lady's auspicious and ochry silk apparel with red rouches...

glosses.meaning: on mountain's, top, when she is staying [strolling]
ochry, with red, having such rouches, auspicious, [silky] apparel

verses.devanagari:
स ददर्श ततः तस्या वृत्तौ ऊरू सुसंहतौ |
स्तनौ च पीनौ सहितौ सुजातम् चारु च आननम्
verses.iast:
sa dadarśa tataḥ tasyā vṛttau ūrū susaṃhatau |
stanau ca pīnau sahitau sujātam cāru ca ānanam
verses.translation: "Then the Air-god beheld her well-twinned, thickset, roundish thighs, and even the paired off plumpish breasts, and her beautiful face which is well proportioned in its build...

verses.devanagari:
ताम् बलात् आयत श्रोणीम् तनु मध्याम् यशस्विनीम् |
दृष्ट्वा एव शुभ सर्वान्गीम् पवनः काम मोहितः
verses.iast:
tām balāt āyata śroṇīm tanu madhyām yaśasvinīm |
dṛṣṭvā eva śubha sarvān.hgīm pavanaḥ kāma mohitaḥ
verses.translation: "Just on catching the sight of that gorgeous one, whose pelvic-girdle is fat and ample and who is slender-waisted, and who by all her limbs is pristine, the Air-god is enamoured...

glosses.meaning: one with - fatly [broad,] ample, pelvic girdle

verses.devanagari:
स ताम् भुजाभ्याम् दीर्घाभ्याम् पर्यष्वजत मारुतः |
मन्मथ आविष्ट सर्वान्गो गत आत्मा ताम् अनिन्दिताम्
verses.iast:
sa tām bhujābhyām dīrghābhyām paryaṣvajata mārutaḥ |
manmatha āviṣṭa sarvān.hgo gata ātmā tām aninditām
verses.translation: "He that Air-god who is ensorcelled by Love-god in all of his limbs, though he is limbless and existing in thin air, embraced that immaculate lady with both of his far-flung arms, as he lost his heart for her...

glosses.meaning: by Love-god, ensorcelled by, in all, limbs

verses.devanagari:
सा तु तत्र एव संभ्रांता सुवृत्ता वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् |
एक पत्नी व्रतम् इदम् को नाशयितुम् इच्छति
verses.iast:
sā tu tatra eva sambhrāṃtā suvṛttā vākyam abravīt |
eka patnī vratam idam ko nāśayitum icchati
verses.translation: "But she that conscientious lady perplexedly said this sentence in that matter of invisible hugging, 'who wishes to despoil my vow of one-man-one-wife...'

glosses.meaning: this, single, wifehood, vow - one-man-one-wife principle of mine

verses.devanagari:
अंजनाया वचः श्रुत्वा मारुतः प्रत्यभाषत |
न त्वाम् हिंसामि सुश्रोणि मा भूत् ते मनसोइ भयम्
verses.iast:
aṃjanāyā vacaḥ śrutvā mārutaḥ pratyabhāṣata |
na tvām hiṃsāmi suśroṇi mā bhūt te manasoi bhayam
verses.translation: "On listening the words of Anjana the Air-god spoke this in reply, 'oh, high-hipped one, I don't dishonour you, hence let there be no fear in your heart, for I am the all-permeating Air-god...

glosses.meaning: to your, heart, fear, let not, be there.

verses.devanagari:
मनसा अस्मि गतो यत् त्वाम् परिष्वज्य यशस्विनि |
वीर्यवान् बुद्धि संपन्नः पुत्रः तव भविष्यति
verses.iast:
manasā asmi gato yat tvām pariṣvajya yaśasvini |
vīryavān buddhi sampannaḥ putraḥ tava bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: " 'By which reason I embraced you and impregnate myself within you, by that reason you are impregnated in a supersensory manner, thereby you will beget a valiant son endowed with intellect...

verses.devanagari:
महासात्त्वो महातेज महाबल पराक्रमः |
लंघने प्लवने चैव भविष्यति मया समः
verses.iast:
mahāsāttvo mahāteja mahābala parākramaḥ |
laṃghane plavane caiva bhaviṣyati mayā samaḥ
verses.translation: " 'An admirably brave, and a bravely dazzling, and a dazzlingly forceful, and a forcefully overpowering son will be there, also thus, he will be a coequal of mine in flying off and jumping up...' Thus, the Air-god said to Anjana.

glosses.meaning: bravely [formal: splendid, spectacular - make a brave show,] dazzling
in fly off, jump off, also thus

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्ता ततः तुष्टा जननी ते महाकपेः |
गुहायाम् त्वाम् महाबाहो प्रजज्ञे प्लवगर्षभ
verses.iast:
evam uktā tataḥ tuṣṭā jananī te mahākapeḥ |
guhāyām tvām mahābāho prajajñe plavagarṣabha
verses.translation: "Oh, arcane monkey Hanuma, when Air-god said so to her, oh, ambidextrous one, your mother is gratified, and then, oh, bullish fly-jumpers, your mother very well divined you in a cave...

glosses.meaning: that way, when she is said [by Air-god]
very, well, divined [tr. discover by guessing, intuition, inspiration, or magic - not a uterine birth.]

verses.devanagari:
अभ्युत्थितम् ततः सूर्यम् बालो दृष्ट्वा महा वने |
फलंचेतिजिघृक्षुस्त्वमुत्प्लुत्याभ्युत्पतोदिवम् - यद्वा -
फलम् च इति जिघृक्षुः त्वम् उत्प्लुत्य अभिउत्पतो दिवम्
verses.iast:
abhyutthitam tataḥ sūryam bālo dṛṣṭvā mahā vane |
phalañcetijighṛkṣustvamutplutyābhyutpatodivam - yadvā -
phalam ca iti jighṛkṣuḥ tvam ut.hplutya abhiutpato divam
verses.translation: "Thereafter, when you were a boy you have see the just risen sun in the vast of forest, and deeming it to be a just ripen reddish fruit, and thinking it to be a best catch, you hopped up and flew towards sun on the sky...

glosses.meaning: thinking it to be a best catch
towards, on, fell up - flew up.

verses.devanagari:
शतानि त्रीणि गत्वा अथ योजनानाम् महाकपे |
तेजसा तस्य निर्धूतो न विषादम् ततो गतः
verses.iast:
śatāni trīṇi gatvā atha yojanānām mahākape |
tejasā tasya nirdhūto na viṣādam tato gataḥ
verses.translation: "Even on your flying up three hundred yojana-s, oh, brave monkey, and even when sun's radiation puffed and blown you down, you did not get into any anguish as were indefatigable...

glosses.meaning: yojana-s, three, hundreds, on going [on flying up]
by radiation, [though] puffed and blown down
by it, into anguish [scare,] not, you got into [you were indefatigably courageous.]

verses.devanagari:
त्वाम् अपि उपगतम् तूर्णम् अंतरीक्षम् महाकपे |
क्षिप्तम् इन्द्रेण ते वज्रम् कोप आविष्टेन तेजसा
verses.iast:
tvām api upagatam tūrṇam aṃtarīkśam mahākape |
kṣiptam indreṇa te vajram kopa āviṣṭena tejasā
verses.translation: "Oh, mighty monkey, even on seeing you who are coming near the vault of heaven, Indra is captivated by anger and by his effulgence he catapulted his Thunderbolt at you...

glosses.meaning: one who with - anger, captivated by

verses.devanagari:
तदा शैलाग्र शिखरे वामो हनुर् अभज्यत |
ततो हि नाम धेयम् ते हनुमान् इति कीर्तितम्
verses.iast:
tadā śailāgra śikhare vāmo hanur abhajyata |
tato hi nāma dheyam te hanumān iti kīrtitam
verses.translation: "Then, your left cheekbone, zygomatic arch, is broken when you fell down on a highest mountaintop, from thereupon your name-phrase is indeed averred as Hanumaan...
notes: The word hanu also means 'wisdom...' and Hanuma is one having an absolute wisdom. He is also addressed as Hanumanta, Hanuma and at certain places Valmiki terms him as Hani... nectareous...

glosses.meaning: then, on mountaintop, highest one [after your falling on it]

verses.devanagari:
ततः त्वाम् निहतम् दृष्ट्वा वायुः गन्ध वहः स्वयम् |
त्रैलोक्यम् भृश संक्रुद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभंजनः
verses.iast:
tataḥ tvām nihatam dṛṣṭvā vāyuḥ gandha vahaḥ svayam |
trailokyam bhṛśa saṃkruddho na vavau vai prabhaṃjanaḥ
verses.translation: "Then on observing that you are mutilated, highly infuriated is that scent-wafter Air-god and that tempestuous Air-god has not physically circulated throughout the triad of worlds...

glosses.meaning: in their entirety, breaker - of trees etc., by his wind-storms, tempestuous Air-god

verses.devanagari:
संभ्रांताः च सुराः सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति |
प्रसादयन्ति संक्रुद्धम् मारुतम् भुवनेश्वराः
verses.iast:
sambhrāṃtāḥ ca surāḥ sarve trailokye kṣubhite sati |
prasādayanti saṅkruddham mārutam bhuvaneśvarāḥ
verses.translation: "When the triad of worlds is being roiled with breathlessness, all the administrative gods of universe are bewildered, and they started to supplicate the Air-god for his grace...

glosses.meaning: triad of worlds, roiled, while being
enraged, Air-god, started to supplicate for grace.

verses.devanagari:
प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यम् वरम् ददौ |
अशस्त्र वध्यताम् तात समरे सत्य विक्रम
verses.iast:
prasādite ca pavane brahmā tubhyam varam dadau |
aśastra vadhyatām tāta samare satya vikrama
verses.translation: "Oh, chivalric warrior at war, while the Air-god is being supplicated, oh, dear boy, Brahma gave you a boon decreeing your 'indestructibility by any missile...'

glosses.meaning: oh, one - in war, chivalric, warrior - Hanuma

verses.devanagari:
वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजम् त्वाम् समीक्ष्य च |
सहस्र नेत्रः प्रीत आत्मा ददौ ते वरम् उत्तमम्
स्वच्छंदतः च मरणम् तव स्यात् इति वै प्रभो |
verses.iast:
vajrasya ca nipātena virujam tvām samīkṣya ca |
sahasra netraḥ prīta ātmā dadau te varam uttamam
svacchaṃdataḥ ca maraṇam tava syāt iti vai prabho |
verses.translation: "On scrutinising that you are unhurt even after hit by Thunderbolt, oh, ablest Hanuma, the Thousand-eyed Indra kind-heartedly gave you a choicest boon saying that your death occurs only by your own volition...

glosses.meaning: of Thunderbolt, falling - on you, hit by it
by volition, death, let there be

verses.devanagari:
स त्वम् केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीम विक्रमः
मारुतस्य औरसः पुत्रः तेजसा च अपि तत् समः |
त्वम् हि वायु सुतो वत्स प्लवने च अपि तत् समः
verses.iast:
sa tvam kesariṇaḥ putraḥ kṣetrajo bhīma vikramaḥ
mārutasya aurasaḥ putraḥ tejasā ca api tat samaḥ |
tvam hi vāyu suto vatsa plavane ca api tat samaḥ
verses.translation: "Such as you are, you are Kesari's son through his wife, oh, frightful pugilist, and you are the lineal son of Air-god, and even by your gusting you are selfsame to Air-god, and even by your flying also you are his selfsame to Air-god, in all respects...
notes: There used to be many systems to beget children in the bygone eras, called kśetraja, one's own, aurasa, in one's own wife but by other supernatural entities, niyoga, in one's own though other superior human beings or supernatural beings, and kṛtrima, by artificial methods like the present day cloning or by 'test tube baby' methods, and by datta, adaptation etc. Here Hanuma is said to be both the kśetraja as well as aurasa where his aurasa sonship is said for its gauṇa artha latent and incidental meaning to endow him with the attributes of Air-god. Dharmaakuutam narrates about these system and some of it is: atra maaruta aurasatvam maaruta viirya utpannatva maatreNa gauNam bodhyam | sa~NskR^ite sva kShetre sva viiryaat utpannasya aurasa shabda mukhya arthatvaat | tathaa ca aurasa aadi vibhaaga pratipaadanam upassaram tallakShaNam darshitaani manunaa - aurasa kShetrajaH caiva dattaH kR^itrima eva ca | guuDHotpannao apaviddhaH ca daayaasaa baandhavaaH ca ShaT || - teShaam lakShaNaani api sa eva aaha - sva kShetre sa~NskR^itaayaam tu svayam utpaaditaH ca yaH | tam aurasamvijaaniiyaat putram prathama kalpitam || sva dharmeNa niyuktaayaam kShetrajaH smR^itaH | sadR^isham priiti samyuktam sa j~neyaH kR^itrimaH sutaH | manu -- And these systems of begetting children is a taboo and banned for this Kali Yuga era: eteṣu datta aurasa vyatiriktānām putratve parigraḥ kalau niṣiddhaḥ | candrika smṛti artha sāra ādau kali yuga dharma madhye parigaṇanāt - iti;And the verse 20 says that Anjana has 'divined Hanuma...' pra ja jñe = very, well, divined... [tr. discover by guessing, intuition, inspiration, or magic]; but not 'delivered' manually through routine labour.

atra maaruta aurasatvam maaruta viirya utpannatva maatreNa gauNam bodhyam | sa~NskR^ite sva kShetre sva viiryaat utpannasya aurasa shabda mukhya arthatvaat | tathaa ca aurasa aadi vibhaaga pratipaadanam upassaram tallakShaNam darshitaani manunaa - aurasa kShetrajaH caiva dattaH kR^itrima eva ca | guuDHotpannao apaviddhaH ca daayaasaa baandhavaaH ca ShaT || - teShaam lakShaNaani api sa eva aaha - sva kShetre sa~NskR^itaayaam tu svayam utpaaditaH ca yaH | tam aurasamvijaaniiyaat putram prathama kalpitam || sva dharmeNa niyuktaayaam kShetrajaH smR^itaH | sadR^isham priiti samyuktam sa j~neyaH kR^itrimaH sutaH | manu -- And these systems of begetting children is a taboo and banned for this Kali Yuga era: eteṣu datta aurasa vyatiriktānām putratve parigraḥ kalau niṣiddhaḥ | candrika smṛti artha sāra ādau kali yuga dharma madhye parigaṇanāt - iti;And the verse 20 says that Anjana has 'divined Hanuma...' pra ja jñe = very, well, divined... [tr. discover by guessing, intuition, inspiration, or magic]; but not 'delivered' manually through routine labour.
eteShu datta aurasa vyatiriktaanaam putratve parigraH kalau niShiddhaH | candrika smR^iti artha saara aadau kali yuga dharma madhye parigaNanaat - iti;

glosses.meaning: one who is - frightful, venturer [fist fighter - pugilist]
arable, born [wife's son, where wife is an arable land, and its crop is his son]
in flying, his [Air-god's,] selfsame, in all respects.

verses.devanagari:
वयम् अद्य गत प्राणा भवान् अस्मासु सांप्रतम् |
दाक्ष्य विक्रम संपन्नः कपि राज इव अपरः
verses.iast:
vayam adya gata prāṇā bhavān asmāsu sāmpratam |
dākṣya vikrama sampannaḥ kapi rāja iva aparaḥ
verses.translation: "Presently we are as good as dead, and among us presently you are the only one rife with competence and valiance, you are the other Sugreeva, the king of monkeys, to us...

glosses.meaning: now, we are [I am,] gone, lives [as good as dead]

verses.devanagari:
त्रिविक्रमे मया तात स शैल वन कानना |
त्रिः सप्त कृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्
verses.iast:
trivikrame mayā tāta sa śaila vana kānanā |
triḥ sapta kṛtvaḥ pṛthivī parikrāntā pradakṣiṇam
verses.translation: "During the period of Trivikrama incarnation I have circumambulated the earth inclusive of its mountains, forests and thickets for twenty-one times, moving rightward around it...

glosses.meaning: in Trivikrama [during the period of incarnation]
three*seven = twenty-one, times, on making - multiplying

verses.devanagari:
तथा च ओषधयो अस्माभिः संचिता देव शासनात् |
निर्मथ्यम् अमृतम् याभिः तदा तदानीम् नो महत् बलम्
verses.iast:
tathā ca oṣadhayo asmābhiḥ saṃcitā deva śāsanāt |
nirmathyam amṛtam yābhiḥ tadā tadānīm no mahat balam
verses.translation: "Like that, by the order of gods we ourselves have collected those herbal plants with which ambrosia had to be churned from Milky Ocean, and in that way, then there used to be a great energy for us...
notes: The expressions 'we' and 'us' 'ourselves' are royal the 'we-s', 'us-s' and 'ourselves...'

glosses.meaning: for us [to me, there used to be] great, energy.

verses.devanagari:
स इदानीम् अहम् वृद्धः परिहीन पराक्रमः |
साम्प्रतम् कालम् अस्माकम् भवान् सर्व गुण अन्वितः
verses.iast:
sa idānīm aham vṛddhaḥ parihīna parākramaḥ |
sāmpratam kālam asmākam bhavān sarva guṇa anvitaḥ
verses.translation: "Such as I am, I am now aged and my valiance is completely lessened... but at the present time, you alone are endowed with all endowments among us...

verses.devanagari:
तत् विजृंभस्व विक्रांतः प्लवताम् उत्तमो हि असि |
त्वत् वीर्यम् द्रष्टु कामा इयम् सर्वा वानर वाहिनी
verses.iast:
tat vijṛmbhasva vikrāṃtaḥ plavatām uttamo hi asi |
tvat vīryam draṣṭu kāmā iyam sarvā vānara vāhinī
verses.translation: "Thereby oh, vanquisher Hanuma, you give a jump-start to leap the ocean. Indeed, you alone are the best one among all fly-jumpers, and this entire vanara army is anxious to witness your prowess...

glosses.meaning: give a jump-start - to leap ocean
among fly-jumpers, the best, you are, indeed

verses.devanagari:
उत्तिष्ठ हरि शार्दूल लंघयस्व महा अर्णवम् |
परा हि सर्व भूतानाम् हनुमन् या गतिः तव
verses.iast:
uttiṣṭha hari śārdūla laṃghayasva mahā arṇavam |
parā hi sarva bhūtānām hanuman yā gatiḥ tava
verses.translation: "Arise, oh, lion-like monkey, leap over this vast ocean, oh, Hanuma, your escape velocity is indeed unalike that of all the other beings...

glosses.meaning: which, cruise [escape velocity = the minimum velocity needed to escape from the gravitational field of a body]
all, beings - escape velocity of all beings

verses.devanagari:
विषाण्णा हरयः सर्वे हनुमन् किम् उपेक्षसे |
विक्रमस्व महावेग विष्णुः त्रीन् विक्रमान् इव
verses.iast:
viṣāṇṇā harayaḥ sarve hanuman kim upekṣase |
vikramasva mahāvega viṣṇuḥ trīn vikramān iva
verses.translation: "Oh, Hanuma, all these monkeys are dispirited. Why this indolence of yours? You boldly triumph over the ocean as your speed is highest, supersonic, super-photic, super-cerebric is your celerity. As with Vishnu who trod the triad of worlds in a trice, you too triumph over..." Thus Jambavanta persuaded Hanuma to get ready for action.
notes: The bracketed words are in remembrance of the regularly chanted eulogy of Hanuma:
manojavam māruta tulya vegam jitendriyam buddhimatām variṣṭham | vātāatmajam vānara yūdha mukhyam śrī rāma dūtam śirasā namāmi ||in that mano javam is 'speedier than thought...'

glosses.meaning: highly, speedy [speedier than sound, light and thought - supersonic, super-photic, super-cerebric
Vishnu, three [who trod the triad of worlds in a trice,] trod, as with
boldly, triumph over. {(aadaraartham punarukti) vi kramasva = boldly, triumph over.]}

verses.devanagari:
ततः कपीनाम् ऋषभेण चोदितः
प्रतीत वेगः पवन आत्मजः कपिः |
प्रहर्षयन् ताम् हरि वीर वाहिनीम्
चकार रूपम् महत् आत्मनः तदा
verses.iast:
tataḥ kapīnām ṛṣabheṇa coditaḥ
pratīta vegaḥ pavana ātmajaḥ kapiḥ |
praharṣayan tām hari vīra vāhinīm
cakāra rūpam mahat ātmanaḥ tadā
verses.translation: Thereafter, when the best monkey among monkeys, namely Jambavanta, the king of bears has motivated, then that son of Air-god, Hanuma, whose speed is familiar coupled with his irresistible enterprise, enormously increased his physique as though to gladded the army of monkeys.

glosses.meaning: thereafter, of monkeys, bullish [Jambavanta] motivated by
familiar, one whose speed [coupled with his irresistible enterprise]
